 On Dec. 25, 2026, HBO and Skydance will dive back into the Wizarding World of Harry Potter with a new reboot series that retells the story from the original novels. Officially titled Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone , this show will move past Daniel Radcliffe's eight movies, bringing newcomer Dominic McLaughlin in to play The Boy Who Lived for a new audience. The series is already building massive anticipation, as its trailers have broken HBO viewing records .

 Marketing for this show ramped up with the release of the first trailer in Mar. 2026 , giving audiences the first look at McLaughlin donning the Hogwarts robes and the lightning scar. A more dialogue-heavy trailer was released in Sept. 2026, teasing more details from the books and showcasing stars like John Lithgow as Albus Dumbledore, Janet McTeer as Minerva McGonagall, and Paapa Essiedu as Severus Snape. Now, more of that story is being teased in never-before-seen footage.
 HBO officially released the first full clip from the upcoming Harry Potter reboot. This clip highlights the first day of school at Hogwarts, as Harry and his friends take part in their first Welcoming Feast after being sorted into their houses. As Harry sees the magic of Hogwarts for the first time, Professor Dumbledore (John Lithgow) and Professor McGonagall (Janet McTeer) express awe over Harry's resemblance to his late father, James, after McGonagall celebrates his placement into Gryffindor House.

 While more action-filled and dramatic footage is sure to come when the show debuts, this clip teases some of the intense VFX work that will go into this series. Bringing a very different look to the feast than in 2001's Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone , the series will also go into much more depth and detail in scenes like this, with a runtime that more than doubles the original movie's 152 minutes .

 From here, only about six weeks remain until the series gets its Christmas release, unveiling HBO's work on the second live-action iteration of this story. While there is still plenty of controversy surrounding the series , centered on book author J.K. Rowling and the response to some of the show's casting decisions, HBO is banking on the reboot being a success. Considering Season 2 is already greenlit and filming, plenty is riding on Season 1 being a big hit for the streamer.
